why: containers are drawn as a panel of machines, not a list — the docker view reads the tile fields, and the launcher still needs title and subtitle for recents and frecency
running first, restarting next, stopped last — band is the sort key and the colour of the tile's edge
within a band the ps order survives — ps listed web before db
a crash loop is something you came to deal with — restarting sits between running and stopped, and the tile carries the count and the exit it keeps dying on
the primary action is the log tail, and the first action carries the enter key
a wildcard bind reads as localhost and opens in a browser; an IPv6 literal needs brackets or nobody can parse the URL
the browser exec is the script's verbatim — omarchy-launch-browser on the quoted url
a known database port is copied, not opened — 5432 is on the deny list, and guessing wrong costs a dead browser tab
Shell Inside exists only where a shell could — a running container gets it
a stopped tile has no shell — there is nothing to exec into
stop, not start, for a container in a crash loop — it is already trying to run and stopping it is the thing you came to do
a failed verb lands in a notification rather than failing invisibly once the launcher has closed
a meter needs its denominator named — a 512MiB cap is a limit, no cap is the host
an unlimited container is drawn against the whole machine and the tile says so
a word after the colon filters by name, so docker:db is one row and not a list to read
ports are in the haystack — docker:8080 is you knowing which port answers and wanting the container behind it
the compose service name reaches the container even when the container's own name never said it
a filter that matches no container answers nothing rather than falling back to every container
the when gate is a live daemon, not a binary on PATH — a machine with docker installed and the daemon stopped shows nothing, not an error
